content: Ranitidine is a medication prescribed to treat ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. GERD is a condition where stomach acid flows backward into the esophagus, causing heartburn and potential damage to the esophageal lining. Over-the-counter ranitidine is also used to prevent and treat symptoms of heartburn associated with acid indigestion and sour stomach. Ranitidine belongs to a class of medications called H2 blockers, which work by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Ranitidine is available in various forms, including tablets, effervescent tablets, effervescent granules, and syrup, all of which are taken orally. It is typically taken once daily at bedtime or two to four times a day, depending on the condition being treated. Over-the-counter ranitidine is usually taken once or twice daily. To prevent heartburn symptoms, it should be taken 30 to 60 minutes before consuming foods or beverages that trigger heartburn. Always follow the instructions on your prescription or the package label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take ranitidine exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. Effervescent tablets and granules should be dissolved in a full glass of water (6–8 ounces) before consumption. Do not use over-the-counter ranitidine for more than two weeks unless advised by your doctor. If symptoms of heartburn, acid indigestion, or sour stomach persist beyond two weeks, discontinue use and contact your doctor. Ranitidine is sometimes used for other purposes, such as treating upper gastrointestinal bleeding, preventing stress ulcers, protecting the stomach from damage caused by nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and reducing the risk of stomach acid aspiration during anesthesia. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of using this medication for your specific condition with your doctor. Ranitidine may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking ranitidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ranitidine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin) and triazolam. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of porphyria, phenylketonuria, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking ranitidine, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking ranitidine. If you miss a dose of ranitidine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Ranitidine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: headache, constipation, diarrhea, upset stomach, vomiting, or stomach pain. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Store ranitidine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on the safe disposal of medications. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking ranitidine. Inform your doctor and laboratory personnel that you are using this medication before undergoing any laboratory tests. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
